angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 235,147 km at 41.31 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 24.2073 +/- 0.0168 mas (same row, RUWE 1.58): 41.31 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.338 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1743 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract): 235,147 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.339 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1743 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3277 +/- 78 K from Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1743 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Yalçinkaya et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1743 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...702A.209Y/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1743.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.910, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
